_comment: Notes shown on an object's panel. 'noExample': why there is no example (shown instead of 'No example yet'). 'note': a caveat shown with the example. Each reason was found while writing the examples; see the PR for evidence. 'graphOnly': objects the browser can run but not as Max does; their examples show the patch and play nothing, and the reason is shown with them. Examples that use an object the browser can't run at all are graph-only without being listed.

noExample.play~: It plays a buffer~, and buffer~ holds only silence in this browser player. It works in Max.
noExample.groove~: It plays a buffer~, and buffer~ holds only silence in this browser player. It works in Max.
noExample.record~: This browser player doesn't write recorded sound into buffer~ yet. It works in Max.
noExample.wave~: It reads a buffer~, and buffer~ holds only silence in this browser player. It works in Max.
noExample.2d.wave~: It reads a buffer~, and buffer~ holds only silence in this browser player. It works in Max.
noExample.pow~: The browser player swaps pow~'s base and exponent, so no example would sound the same here as in Max.
noExample.teeth~: The browser player reads teeth~'s arguments differently from Max (samples instead of milliseconds), so no example would be correct in both.
noExample.past: maxpylang requires two arguments for past, which changes what it does in Max, so no example would be correct in both.
noExample.router: The browser player numbers router's inlets and outlets from 1 and Max from 0, so no example would route the same way in both.
noExample.histo: The browser player swaps histo's two outlets, so no example would be correct in both.
noExample.dict.pack: The browser player's dict.pack takes key-value messages, where Max has one inlet per key, so no example would be correct in both.
noExample.dict.unpack: The browser player's dict.unpack sends key-value messages, where Max has one outlet per key, so no example would be correct in both.
noExample.dict.route: The browser player's dict.route splits by key names, where Max compares against a dictionary, so no example would be correct in both.
noExample.dict.iter: Every dictionary source works differently in the browser player and in Max, so no example would be correct in both.
noExample.dict.join: Every dictionary source works differently in the browser player and in Max, so no example would be correct in both.
noExample.dict.strip: Every dictionary source works differently in the browser player and in Max, so no example would be correct in both.
noExample.dict.serialize: Every dictionary source works differently in the browser player and in Max, so no example would be correct in both.
noExample.dict.deserialize: The browser player only reads a single JSON string, which a Max message box can't make, so no example would be correct in both.
noExample.umenu: The browser player reads umenu's items from the box text, and maxpylang stores them as an attribute, so the menu would show one item reading "umenu".
noExample.tab: The browser player reads tab's items from the box text, and maxpylang stores them as an attribute, so it would show one tab reading "tab".
noExample.mc.play~: It plays a buffer~, and buffer~ holds only silence in this browser player. It works in Max.
noExample.mc.groove~: It plays a buffer~, and buffer~ holds only silence in this browser player. It works in Max.
noExample.mc.wave~: It plays a buffer~, and buffer~ holds only silence in this browser player. It works in Max.
noExample.mc.playlist~: maxpylang can't store mc.playlist~'s clips in the patch yet.
noExample.mc.pow~: The browser player swaps pow~'s base and exponent, so no example would sound the same here as in Max.
noExample.mc.line: maxpylang gives mc.line a different number of outlets from Max, and the browser player treats it as plain line.
noExample.patcher: maxpylang places p (patcher) as an empty subpatcher with no inlets or outlets, and can't put objects inside it, so nothing can be connected to it. Build an abstraction instead: see the inlet and outlet examples.
noExample.bpatcher: maxpylang places bpatcher with no inlets or outlets, even when it names a patch file, so nothing can be connected to it. Use an abstraction instead: see the inlet and outlet examples.
noExample.js: maxpylang writes a js box as js 1 1 file.js, with the inlet and outlet counts before the file name, and Max may not find the script in a box like that (see known issues). An example here would teach a box that may not load.
noExample.mc.gen~: maxpylang places mc.gen~ without the gen patch inside it, so what it does depends on code you write in Max. Open it in Max to write that code.
noExample.p: maxpylang places p (patcher) as an empty subpatcher with no inlets or outlets, and can't put objects inside it, so nothing can be connected to it. Build an abstraction instead: see the inlet and outlet examples.
noExample.cpuclock: cpuclock reports the time, in milliseconds, when banged. On its own it makes no sound, and to time events, timer is simpler (see timer).
noExample.closebang: closebang sends a bang when the patch closes, so there is nothing to see or hear while it plays. Connect it to whatever should happen on closing.
noExample.freebang: freebang sends a bang when its box is deleted or the patch closes, so there is nothing to see or hear while it plays.
noExample.hint: hint is a box of text shown on the patch; it doesn't send or change anything.
noExample.bgcolor: bgcolor sets a patch's background colour (in old patches; today's Max sets it in the patch's settings). It doesn't send or change anything.
noExample.combine: combine joins numbers and words into one word (a symbol), such as a file name. On its own it makes no sound; an example would only show text.

note.notein: In Max this reads your MIDI keyboard. This browser player doesn't read MIDI devices yet, so here you hear the default sound.
note.ctlin: In Max this reads your MIDI controller. This browser player doesn't read MIDI devices yet, so here you hear the default sound.
note.bendin: In Max this reads your pitch-bend wheel. This browser player doesn't read MIDI devices yet, so here you hear the default sound.
note.pgmin: In Max this reads program changes from your MIDI device. This browser player doesn't read MIDI devices yet, so here you hear the default sound.
note.key: Click the page outside the code first: typing in the code editor plays notes too.
note.keyup: Click the page outside the code first: typing in the code editor plays notes too.
note.jit.grab: Uses your camera: your browser will ask first.
note.jit.matrix: Uses your camera. The browser player reads jit.matrix's size differently from Max, so the picture may look different here.
note.jit.window: Uses your camera: your browser will ask first.
note.jit.pwindow: Uses your camera: your browser will ask first.
note.jit.brcosa: Uses your camera. The browser player ignores @brightness, @contrast and @saturation, so here the picture is unchanged; in Max it turns black and white.
note.jit.scalebias: Uses your camera. The browser player ignores @scale and @bias, so here the picture is unchanged; in Max it fades to grey.
note.jit.3m: Uses your camera. Written for the browser player, whose jit.3m sends one brightness value per outlet; Max sends a list per plane, in a different order.

graphOnly.buffer~: In this browser player, buffer~ holds only silence: it can't load a file, and record~ doesn't write into it yet. In Max this plays.
graphOnly.mc.2d.wave~: It plays a buffer~, and buffer~ holds only silence in this browser player. In Max this plays.
graphOnly.mc.record~: This browser player doesn't write recorded sound into buffer~ yet. In Max this records.
graphOnly.dict: The browser player's dict sends values and dictionaries out of different outlets from Max, so this example plays only in Max.
graphOnly.inlet: An inlet or outlet object makes a port on an abstraction (a patch saved to its own file and placed by name in another patch). This browser player can't run abstractions yet, so this example shows the patch and plays nothing. In Max it plays.
graphOnly.outlet: An inlet or outlet object makes a port on an abstraction (a patch saved to its own file and placed by name in another patch). This browser player can't run abstractions yet, so this example shows the patch and plays nothing. In Max it plays.
graphOnly.bondo: This browser player's bondo sends its values only when the left inlet gets something; Max's sends them when any inlet does. So this example, written for Max, plays only in Max.
graphOnly.bucket: This browser player's bucket has one outlet, which sends the oldest number; Max's has one outlet per stage. So this example, written for Max, plays only in Max.
graphOnly.offer: This browser player's offer keeps a pair after it is read; Max's forgets it. So this example, written for Max, plays only in Max.
graphOnly.date: This browser player's date answers any bang with the day, month and year; Max's answers date, time and ticks messages. So this example, written for Max, plays only in Max.
graphOnly.active: This browser player has no patch window to come to the front, so active never sends anything here. In Max this plays while the window is in front.
